title: The Secret of the King's Letters
synopsis: A paper in the King's new letters is half burnt.
Only the night guard saw what was on it.
goal: Find out who wrote the burnt paper, and what it says, before the rain.

options.label: The scholars' hall
options.feedback: Scholars write Chinese characters well. They never copy a sign. Read your notes again.

options.label: The guard post
options.feedback: No bucket stands at the guard post, and the drops lead away from it.

options.label: The path to the kitchen well

notes: Picture gate_courtyard (2026-11-04): the scholars' hall doorway (left), the guard post with its brazier (right middle) and the path to the kitchen well with its jars (far right) are drawn in it and measured on this file (grid sheet). The three traces lie on the plain paving in front of the steps.
Traces read (DeductionScene): 門 copied from the gate sign (the writer could not write Chinese characters), a bucket ring and water drops all point to the path to the kitchen well.
The three traces are drawn by the app over their areas (copiedScrap, waterRing, waterDrops): no writing is ever in a picture.

learning.objective: 세종의 말("많은 사람이 하고 싶은 말을 쓰지 못한다")과 흔적 문장을 읽고, 한자를 쓰지 못한 사람이 어디서 왔는지 추리한다.
expressions: Many people cannot write what they want to say.

play.title: The Paper Under the Gate
story: The paper is half burnt. Only one mark is left on it: a small ring.
Who left a paper under the gate at night?
play.letter:
The King said: "Many people cannot write what they want to say."
Someone copied 門 from the gate sign, three times.
A wet ring: a water bucket stood here.
Drops of water lead away from the gate.
play.question: Where did the writer come from? Tap the place.
hints: Tap the paper scrap, the wet ring and the drops of water.
Who carries water in the palace?
play.successMessage: The writer carries water from the kitchen well!
transition: At the well, the water-carriers know the hand at once.
"That is Bun-i," says one. "She went home at sunset."
"Sora, the palace maid, teaches her the new letters."

talk.speaker: taek
talk.goal: Find out where Taek found the paper.

lines.text: It was under the inner gate after sunset.
Strange little marks. Boxes, rings, a tooth or two. I thought it was a game.
Then someone wrote it before the gate closed.

clue.title: The Writer
clue.note: Bun-i carries water. She could not write Chinese characters, so she tried the new letters.

evidence.name: The Copied Scrap
evidence.description: 門 copied three times from the gate sign. The writer could not write Chinese characters.

notes: Taek names each group by the body part Sora's board gives it (teeth, back of the tongue, mouth, throat), never by its shape: the board's English decides the letter, a Korean reader's eye alone does not.
Four letters are not in the note (ㄴ ㅁ ㅊ ㅍ): 'one step stronger' is one more line (the board's rule, shown with ㄴ ㄷ ㅌ only), so ㅈ not ㅊ, ㅂ not ㅍ or ㅁ, and the back of the tongue ㄱ not ㄴ.
Letters are tiles of the app (text): never in a picture.

clueInputs.note: Bun-i wrote the paper; Sora teaches her.

learning.objective: 택이 말한 발음 기관(teeth, back of the tongue, mouth, throat)과 '한 단계 센 소리(one step stronger)'를 글자판의 영어 설명(copies the ..., a stronger sound adds one line)에 맞춰 방해 글자 사이에서 자음 다섯을 순서대로 고른다.
expressions: A stronger sound adds one line.

play.title: Sora's Lesson Box
story: Sora comes to the well with a lamp.
"Bun-i learned the new letters in ten days," she says.
"My pupils lock their slates in my lesson box with a new word's sounds."
Sora reads her board out loud. Taek listens, and he remembers the marks he saw.
play.letterIntro: Sora's lesson board, and Taek's memory:
play.letter:
Sora's board: ㄱ copies the back of the tongue. ㄴ copies the tongue on the gums.
ㅁ copies the mouth. ㅅ copies the teeth. ㅇ copies the throat.
A stronger sound adds one line: ㄴ, then ㄷ, then ㅌ.
Taek: "Group 1 was the teeth."
"Group 2 was the back of the tongue."
"Group 3 was the teeth, one step stronger."
"Group 4 was the mouth, one step stronger. The throat was under it."
play.question: Which letters did Bun-i write? Tap them in Taek's order.
hints: Find the teeth and the back of the tongue on Sora's board.
One step stronger is one more line: ㄴ becomes ㄷ, not ㅌ.
play.orderFeedback: Those are the right letters. Read Taek's groups again, one by one.

feedback.siot,giyeok,chieut,bieup,ieung: Group 3 is the teeth one step stronger: one more line, not two.
feedback.siot,giyeok,jieut,pieup,ieung: Group 4 is the mouth one step stronger: one more line, not two.
feedback.siot,giyeok,jieut,mieum,ieung: Group 4 is the mouth one step stronger: it has one more line.
feedback.siot,nieun,jieut,bieup,ieung: Group 2 is the back of the tongue, not the tongue on the gums.

transition: Inside is Bun-i's slate, with the same five sounds.
But the lines and dots between them are wiped away.
"Taek, what did the rest look like?" Sora asks.

talk.speaker: sora
talk.goal: Find out how Bun-i learned to write.

lines.text: The King asked me a question: can ordinary people learn his letters in ten days?
Bun-i could not write one Chinese character. Today was her tenth day.
Then the marks Taek saw are her letters.

clue.title: The Sounds
clue.note: The teeth, the back of the tongue, the teeth one step stronger, the mouth one step stronger, and the throat under it.

evidence.name: Sora's Lesson Board
evidence.description: The first letters copy the tongue, the mouth, the teeth and the throat. A stronger sound adds a line.

notes: Each group's vowel built from Taek's words: ㅓ (dot left of a standing line), ㅗ (dot on a flat line), ㅣ, ㅜ (dot under a flat line); each first sound is chosen from M2's by its body part. The note reads 서고 지붕, the book hall roof.

The paper holds the groups as Bun-i wrote them: down the page, two to a column, the first column on the right (columnHeight 2). Its places are named TOP RIGHT, BOTTOM RIGHT, TOP LEFT, BOTTOM LEFT, never by group number: knowing the words 서고 지붕 is not enough, Sora's English says where each group sits. Written across the page (서고 / 지붕 in rows) the note reads 고붕서지.
Every letter is the app's text (SyllableBoard): never in a picture.

clueInputs.note: The first sounds of Bun-i's groups.

learning.objective: 점(하늘)·누운 줄(땅)·선 줄(사람)과 위치 표현(on its left, on top, under it), 세로쓰기 설명(top to bottom, the first column is on the right)을 읽고 종이 위 제자리에 네 글자를 완성한다.
expressions: a standing line, with a dot on its left
The first column is on the right.

play.title: Four Little Groups
story: Sora takes you to her writing room.
"Our vowels come from three shapes," she says.
"A round dot is the sky. A flat line is the earth. A standing line is a person."
"And we do not write across the page, as you do."
play.letter:
A dot joins a line to make a vowel.
Flat vowels go under the first sound. Standing vowels go on its right.
The sound at the bottom uses the same letters as the first sounds.
We write from top to bottom. The first column is on the right.
Bun-i wrote two groups in each column.
play.question: Build each group in its place on the paper. What did Bun-i write?
hints: Group 1 is at the top right. Group 2 is under it.
Group 3 is at the top of the left column. For each group, choose its sound, then lay its line and its dot.

feedback.고붕서지: Bun-i did not write across the page. Read Sora's lesson: from top to bottom, and the first column is on the right.
feedback.지붕서고: Bun-i's first column is on the right, not on the left.
feedback.사고지붕: Group 1's dot is on the left of its line, not the right.

play.successMessage: The note is whole again. Sora reads it out: "the book hall roof"!
transition: Sora goes pale. "Bun-i saw a hole in the book hall roof!"
"The rain will ruin the books. But the book hall is locked at night."
"Only the King can open it now." The first drops of rain fall.

talk.speaker: taek
talk.goal: Find out what the lines and dots looked like.

lines.text: Each group had lines and dots too. I looked at that paper for a long time.
And the ring on the burnt corner was at the bottom of the last group.

clue.title: Bun-i's Note
clue.note: Bun-i wrote: the book hall roof. She saw a hole in it.

evidence.name: Bun-i's Note
evidence.description: Bun-i's note, put back together from Taek's memory. It names the book hall roof.

blocks.line: Group 1: the teeth. A standing line, with a dot on its left.
Group 2: the back of the tongue. A flat line, with a dot on top.
Group 3: the teeth, one step stronger. Only a standing line.
Group 4: the mouth, one step stronger. A flat line, with a dot under it. The throat's ring sits at the bottom.

notes: King Sejong's three questions, each answered by one mission's evidence: who wrote it (the copied scrap), how she could after ten days (Sora's board), what it says (Bun-i's note). His words are made up (dossier fiction).

clueInputs.note: Bun-i could not write Chinese characters.
The letters copy the mouth: easy to learn.
The note names the book hall roof.

learning.objective: 세종의 세 질문(Who wrote this? How? What does it say?)을 읽고 각 질문에 맞는 증거를 하나씩 보여 준다.

play.title: The King's Letters
story: Rain is falling. Sora sends word to the King.
King Sejong comes to the locked book hall under a paper umbrella.
"A paper in my letters?" he asks. "Show me."
play.letter:
Bun-i could not write Chinese characters.
The first letters copy the mouth. A stronger sound adds a line.
Bun-i's note names the book hall roof.
play.question: Answer the King's three questions with your evidence.
hints: Show one piece of evidence for each question.
Use the copied scrap, Sora's board and Bun-i's note.
transition: Guards open the book hall. Servants hold oiled paper over the hole.
Everyone carries the books out of the rain.
"You learned my letters in one night," says the King. "And Bun-i spoke to me with them."

ending.text: At dawn, Bun-i comes back with her water bucket.

ending.speaker: bun_i
ending.text: The King read my letter? My very first letter?

ending.speaker: sora
ending.text: He did. And he says thank you.

learningGoal.title: Reading how the new letters are made

objectives: Find out who wrote the paper.
Show the King what it says.
intro: Autumn, 1446. You are a guest of King Sejong in Hanyang.
He shows you 28 new letters. "I made them in 1443," he says.
"Our words are not like Chinese words. Many people cannot write what they want to say."
"My scholar says a wise person can learn them in one morning. Can you read them by dawn?"
Later, at the inner gate, Guard Taek lights his lantern with a strange paper.
You pull it out of the fire. Rain clouds are coming.
play.caseSummary: Bun-i wrote her first letter in the new letters. The book hall roof had a hole. King Sejong read it and saved the books.

notes: Seoul Pilot Case 01, redesigned (docs/SEOUL_CASE01_REDESIGN.md, approved 2026-11-04). Test-only: never in the game's season list.
King Sejong appears and speaks: every word of his is made up (dossier fiction), two lines retell his preface (h9, h5). Bun-i, Sora and Taek are made up.
